heading: New engine

basics.name: Engine name
basics.briefHint: Describe the objective, tone, what to say and what to avoid, and any links. This becomes the AI's instructions, so the more specific, the better.
basics.briefPlaceholder: You are re-engaging {{learners}} who stopped attending. Be warm and brief…

dataPoints.intro: Pick the signals the AI may read about each person. More context means smarter, better-timed messages.
dataPoints.consent: I confirm this institute has consent to use the sensitive data points above for messaging.

channels.intro: Which channels can this engine use? Until a channel graduates, you review every message before it sends. WhatsApp needs Meta-approved templates (set up after creating).
channels.auto: Auto-send proactively (after this channel graduates; until then you review and send each one)
channels.autoReply: Auto-answer replies (AI replies within 24h; money, anger, requests to stop and uncertainty always come to you)
channels.autoHint: After this channel graduates; until then you review and send each one.
channels.autoReplyHint: AI replies within 24h; money, anger, requests to stop and uncertainty always come to you.
channels.callNote: The engine proposes a call for your team. Calls are never placed from the task inbox.
channels.whatsappNote: Needs Meta-approved templates — the AI proposes them after you create the engine.

audience.intro: Who should this engine engage? Combine {{batches}} and {{audiences}}. People are de-duplicated automatically.

cadence.recheckHint: A safety floor. The AI decides the actual timing; this caps how often it revisits someone.
cadence.quietHint: No messages between these hours, in the timezone below. The institute's own quiet-hours floor still applies on top of this.

autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.hint: Controls that apply only to channels you set to auto-send.
autonomy.firstNHint: Each auto-send channel stays copilot until you have approved this many of its drafts on that channel; then it starts sending on its own. Leave blank for the default.
autonomy.holdoutHint: A share of the audience (0–100%) that is enrolled but never messaged, so you can measure the engine's real lift against them.

review.name: Name
review.draftNote: The engine starts as a Draft. After creating it, enroll the audience and (for WhatsApp) set up templates, then activate it.

enroll.title: Enroll the audience
enroll.text: Use “Resolve audience” on the engine page to add the people from your sources.

templates.title: Approve WhatsApp templates
templates.text: The AI proposes them; you approve and submit; Meta reviews.

activate.title: Dry run, then activate
activate.text: See simulated drafts in the task inbox before anything goes out.

errors.nameAndBrief: An engine needs a name and a brief.

subtitle: Six short steps. You can review everything before it is created — nothing is sent until you activate it.
